subject: Intermittent 5xx/timeouts from hypatia5b — mitigation & next steps
messages:

Cc: Neptune Alerts <alerts@neptune.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 10:55:00 -0700
Subject: Hypatia5B returning 500/timeouts in prod (urgent)

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a spike of 500s and request timeouts from the hypatia5b endpoint in our production environment starting ~10:40 PDT. Affected requests are ~12-18% of traffic and impact our customer-facing inference pipeline (batch + live). Sample request IDs: req_98765, req_98766, req_98771. Latency jumps to >8s then 502/504/timeout.

This is causing an elevated error rate on our side and several downstream alerts. Can you confirm whether this is a platform-wide issue or something targeted to our account/region? We can provide logs if that helps.

Our team needs an ETA and whether you can route traffic to a fallback model for us temporarily.

Thanks —
Liam Brooks
Platform Engineer, Neptune Analytics
liam.brooks@neptune.ai

Quick triage update (short):

What we see:
- Error spike started ~10:38 PDT and concentrated in a subset of the us-west-2 hypatia5b pool (approx 18% of requests routed to the affected hosts).
- Errors are a mix of 502/504 and timed-out generator loops after multiple KV cache evictions. Sample req ids from Liam match traces we pulled.
- One GPU node group exhibited repeated driver resets and elevated mem pressure leading to request handlers dropping.

Immediate mitigations applied (11:50–12:10 PDT):
1) Opened circuit to affected hosts and temporarily routed ~25% of traffic for Neptune to hypatia5b-quant-fallback. Jonas: note this required a short config flip that added a transient 200ms to median latency.
2) Restarted the agent process on 3 affected instances and evicted problematic cache entries to stabilize memory usage.
3) Prescaled additional healthy capacity in us-west-2 to absorb backlog and reduce queuing.

Current status (12:20 PDT):
- Error rate for Neptune dropped from ~18% -> ~3% after routing and restarts.
- We've scheduled a rolling replacement for the affected node group; engineering is preparing a patch for the driver/kernel handshake that triggered repeated resets.

Next steps (ETA):
- 12:30 PDT: continue to monitor; keep routing in place for now.
- 13:30 PDT: if stable for 1hr, we'll reduce fallback routing to 10% then remove if errors remain <1%.
- Engineering to provide root cause and permanent fix plan by EOD.

Attachments: trace-20280822-usw2.zip (contains sample spans, request ids, and aggregated host metrics).

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hypatia5B returning 500/timeouts in prod (urgent)

Full update and root cause summary:

Summary:
- We traced the immediate root cause to a recent runtime kernel selection change deployed last night (commit 9f3b2c7) that altered attention-kernel fallback heuristics for long-context requests. On certain memory fragmentation patterns this produced higher than expected temporary memory allocations and triggered a driver-level reset on a small percentage of GPUs. When the reset occurred, requests in-flight returned 502/504; repeated attempts produced timeouts.

What we changed (completed 14:40 PDT):
- Reverted the kernel heuristic change for the stable hypatia5b pool (hotfix commit f8d4c0a) and rolled forward to affected clusters.
- Replaced 4 nodes from the problematic driver batch (rolling replace completed at 14:55 PDT).
- Kept Neptune traffic on the quant-fallback for 20% while we validated end-to-end behavior.

Impact and customer visible status:
- As of 15:05 PDT error rate for Neptune is <0.5% and overall latency is back to normal (median within SLA).
- We will keep increased monitoring for 48 hours and run a focused regression test across long-context workloads.

Postmortem plan:
- We'll produce a write-up with timeline, contributing factors, and long-term mitigations (better kernel selection unit tests, memory fragmentation detection, and a safer canary policy). Draft will be posted to INF-2345 and I'll share a customer-friendly summary.

Can we share the postmortem link with Neptune once the doc is in review? Monica, please advise on wording/approvals for public-facing summary.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll follow up with a formal RCA and preventive actions.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Principal Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
